subject: Dedicated capacity recap - Acme Health
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
To: Sam Taylor <sam.taylor@acme-health.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity recap - Acme Health

Sam —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and agreed next steps so everyone is aligned.

Key pain points you shared:
- Latency spikes during morning and evening peaks when clinical workflows hit the API (95th pct latency inconsistent).
- Regulatory/data isolation needs: PHI in inference requests — must be VPC/private deployment with customer-managed keys.
- Throughput unpredictability: current on-prem model struggles to scale during campaign-driven demand.

Goals we outlined:
- Reserve dedicated GPU capacity to guarantee baseline throughput for clinical validation and production traffic.
- Ensure end-to-end data isolation (VPC + KMS/HSM) and audit logs for compliance reviews.
- Able to scale (burst) for periodic campaigns without impacting SLAs.
- Target go-live window: early Oct (you mentioned Oct 1 as preferred).

Proposed Redwood Dedicated configuration (high level):
- Baseline: 8 x A100-equivalent GPU pool (reserved) for model serving (pinned model version).
- Burst capacity: up to 12 GPUs for 48-hour campaign windows (auto-burst subject to availability).
- Network & security: private VPC peering, customer KMS integration (HSM option), audit logs retention 1 year (can adjust).
- SLA targets: 99.9% uptime for dedicated capacity + 1-hour P1 response from our escalation team (we'll include appendix).
- Rollout: canary traffic split, automatic fallback to a compatible model variant for graceful degradation.

Attachments I’m sending after this thread: redwood-dedicated-pricing.xlsx and sow-acme-draft.pdf. I’ll also attach our SOC 2 Type II report for procurement.

Agreed next steps (action items):
1) I’ll send the pricing sheet, SOW draft, and SOC2 PDF by EOD today — (Marissa).
2) Sam to confirm preferred contract term (12 vs 24 months) and confirm final procurement contact (Jordan?) — (Sam).
3) Schedule a 30-min technical kickoff next week with your infra lead + Neha for network/firewall details — propose Wed 7/28 or Thu 7/29.
4) Redwood to prepare SLA appendix and procurement checklist for your legal/procurement review (Rishi/Marissa).

If I missed anything, flag it and I’ll update. Thanks — looking forward to moving this to SOW/PO quickly.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com
+1 (415) 555-0142

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-pricing.xlsx; sow-acme-draft.pdf

From: Sam Taylor <sam.taylor@acme-health.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme-health.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 15:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity recap - Acme Health

Thanks Marissa — this looks good and aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications from procurement/ops side: 

- Contract term: procurement prefers 24 months if we can get a modest discount for the committed baseline. Can you include pricing for both 12 and 24 month terms (with committed baseline of 8 GPUs)?
- SOC2: we need the Type II report and a contact for a security call. Please attach the report and suggest 2x 30-min slots next week for a brief security review.
- Marketplace: Is this available via our AWS Marketplace or GCP Marketplace (would prefer Marketplace procurement if possible).
- PO & signature: Jordan (cc’d) will drive procurement. Please include a procurement checklist we can hand to finance.
- Go-live: Oct 1 is our target — can you confirm onboarding timeline (Neha will coordinate).

I’ll loop in Jordan for technical details post this thread. Thanks — Sam

Sam Taylor
Director of Engineering, Acme Health
sam.taylor@acme-health.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
To: Sam Taylor <sam.taylor@acme-health.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference.com>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme-health.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity recap - Acme Health

Perfect — will do. Quick confirmations:
- I’ll include 12- and 24-month pricing rows in the attached spreadsheet and call out committed baseline discounts.
- Attaching SOC2 Type II and procurement-checklist.xlsx in this thread.
- Marketplace: we support AWS Marketplace for Dedicated for finance-assisted purchases; will note that option in the pricing sheet.
- Onboarding: Neha will share a 6-week onboarding plan (network prep, model pinning, canary testing) in the technical kickoff.

Proposed security call slots: Wed 7/28 10:00-10:30am PT or Thu 7/29 2:00-2:30pm PT — Jordan/your team, let us know which works.

I’ll follow up with the SOW and SLA appendix.

—
Marissa

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference.com>
To: Sam Taylor <sam.taylor@acme-health.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 17:45:00 -0700
Subject: SLA appendix and escalation contacts

Sam —

Following up from Marissa’s recap: we can commit to a 99.9% availability SLA for dedicated capacity with the following escalation path for P1 incidents: 1-hour response, 4-hour mitigation target, and daily updates until resolution. We’ll include an SLA appendix (SLA-appendix.pdf) with remedies and uptime measurement methodology in the SOW packet.

If you’ll be evaluating the 24-month committed option, I can also include a one-time professional services credit for onboarding (covers model pinning and canary rollout support).

We’ll get the full packet to you by EOD (pricing, SOW draft, SOC2, procurement checklist, SLA appendix).

Thanks —
Rishi Malhotra
Sales Director, Redwood Inference
